plugins.description: Oolio Product Management. The full PM toolkit, signal to shipped: feedback intake into JPD, idea grooming to Oolio's standards, PRD writing and grilling, story mockups built in Figma from Oolio components, validation via the Virtual Product Council and its hospitality personas, Jira hygiene, Steering packs, the GTM suite, release notes written in the house voice and verified against what actually shipped, metrics review, discovery maps for themes too big for one session, and the research house: HubSpot/web/Apify signal synthesis, competitor dossiers, sweeps and battlecards, win/loss mining, a daily HubSpot sweep that turns the support queue into cited Insights, one-off evidence attached as native JPD Insights, plus a compass that routes you to the right skill, drive, which turns a raw, rambling request into a finished result, and Roy the Behavioural Alchemist, the behavioural-economics lens, plus the Brain maintenance skills that keep the my_brain knowledge vault compounding, and push-to-brain, the explicit end-of-session push that lands what a session established on the page that already owns it. The QA family tests the built product before it ships: a test basis that lines up the sources and proves the metrics are measurable, functional, exploratory, design-conformance, WCAG 2.2 accessibility, synthetic-persona, code-coverage and resilience passes, real-user UAT, one defect standard that reworks stories before merge, and a release gate whose verdict hands GTM only verified claims and learns from what it missed. Forty-seven skills.

skills.title: Accessibility audit: can everyone use it
skills.lede: Three passes, reported separately, so nobody mistakes an automated pass for conformance. Automated tools catch only part of the issues; keyboard, focus and assistive-technology checks catch the rest. The floor is **WCAG 2.2 AA**, one version ahead of the generic plugin's 2.1, and 2.2's new criteria bite Oolio directly: every drag in a menu builder needs a single-pointer alternative (2.5.7), and sticky control bars and drawers must not hide the focused field (2.4.11).

about.kicker: Every product team has written down how it works. In forty Confluence pages, three stale Notion docs, and one person's head.
lede: Written down is not the same as readable. Readable is not the same as running.

This is ours, readable and running. Every box on this map is one of {skills} real skills, installed by a real person, that an assistant runs against our actual tools. Not a diagram of how we intend to work. The thing itself.

sections.label: Why bother
paragraphs: Product work is a small set of moves repeated forever. Turn signal into a shaped idea. Pressure-test it honestly. Write it down. Decide. Ship it. Find out whether you were right.

Doing those well is not a question of talent. It is a question of discipline, and discipline is the first thing to go when the quarter gets loud. Written down, the standard stops depending on who is having a good week.

sections.label: The people are the point
paragraphs: None of this replaces a product manager. It removes the tax on being one: the blank page, the fourth rewrite, the research you know exists somewhere, the ticket nobody groomed, the decision relitigated because no one recorded it.
What is left is the part that needed a human all along. Judgement. Taste. Knowing which problem deserves the company's next quarter.
The car does not win the race. But nobody wins it in the wrong car.

sections.label: What keeps it honest
list: A person signs off anything that counts. Those are the amber gates, and they do not move.
Findings land in the Brain, so what the team learns compounds instead of restarting.
Nothing reaches Jira or Confluence unreviewed.

sections.label: Reading the map
paragraphs: Left to right is the lifecycle, signal to shipped to learned. Colour is who runs it. The arcs underneath are the loops, which are the reason this is a system and not a pipeline. Click any flow to trace a path end to end.

Lining the sources up first finds those for the price of reading.

catalogue.title: Functional QA
catalogue.blurb: Run a release's acceptance criteria as concrete examples against the live build, in the browser, by role and name, and confirm the analytics events its success metrics need actually fire. Pass, Fail or Blocked per AC with evidence, at least one negative case each, technique chosen by the rule's shape (boundaries, decision tables, state transitions, pairwise). Also re-runs the product area's regression pack. Trigger on "test the ACs", "does it do what the story says", "functional test <story/epic/PR>", "run the regression pack", "check the events fire", "is it instrumented", "verify this fix". Reports through defect-writer, so a failed AC before merge sends the story back for rework.
catalogue.summary: Run a release's acceptance criteria as concrete examples against the live build, in the browser, by role and name, and confirm the analytics events its success metrics need actually fire.
catalogue.lede: Runs every acceptance criterion as a concrete example against the build, and proves the release will produce the data its own success metrics depend on. The question is narrow on purpose: does the build do what the story, the decision log and the PRD's metrics say it must.

catalogue.title: Exploratory QA
catalogue.blurb: Run chartered, timeboxed exploratory testing sessions against a live build to find what breaks off the happy path, the defects nobody wrote an AC for. Charters come from the risk map, the hospitality conditions library (midnight trading days, two managers in two tabs, back button mid-publish, empty venues, big catalogues) and past failures; SFDPOT checks coverage and HICCUPPS recognises problems. Session notes are the evidence. Trigger on "explore this", "try to break it", "exploratory test", "what happens off the happy path", "edge cases on <feature>", "run some charters", "bug bash". Reports through defect-writer.
catalogue.summary: Run chartered, timeboxed exploratory testing sessions against a live build to find what breaks off the happy path, the defects nobody wrote an AC for.
catalogue.lede: Simultaneous learning, test design and execution, with a charter, a timebox and notes, so it is investigation rather than wandering. This is the skill that would have caught "creating a Sat/Sun schedule deletes every existing schedule": a Time × Data charter on overlapping schedules, not an AC anyone wrote.

catalogue.title: Design Conformance
catalogue.blurb: Check that the built screen is what was designed, in the system's own components. Compares the live build, in order, against the Figma frame for the work, the component reference (is this the real ControlBar or a lookalike, are all states present, does the Select follow its rules), the pattern library (navigation in the shell, drawers versus modals, save versus publish, destructive actions, empty and error states), the design tokens, and the glossary. Tags every deviation deliberate, drift or system gap, so drift goes to engineering and gaps go to Design. Trigger on "does the build match the design", "check it against Figma", "design QA", "is this our component", "pass it through design", "check the copy against the glossary".
catalogue.summary: Check that the built screen is what was designed, in the system's own components.
catalogue.lede: The mechanical version of "pass it through the design team". It does not ask whether the design is good; that judgement stays with the Design Council. It asks whether the build is the design, built from the system, using the product's words.
excludes: To judge whether the design itself is good (design-council-review, built mode) or for WCAG checks (accessibility-audit)

catalogue.title: Accessibility Audit
catalogue.blurb: Audit a live build against WCAG 2.2 AA and Oolio's surface targets (POS, kiosk, KDS, back office, online) in three passes reported separately: automated (axe-core rules, contrast on rendered colours), assisted (keyboard-only run of every task, focus not obscured, names and roles from the accessibility tree, target sizes, a single-pointer alternative for every drag, reflow, errors linked to fields) and the human-required list (real screen reader, cognitive load). Produces findings against the success criterion and a VPAT-shaped summary. Trigger on "accessibility audit", "is this accessible", "WCAG check", "keyboard test this", "check contrast", "can everyone use it", "we need an ACR or VPAT".
catalogue.summary: Audit a live build against WCAG 2.2 AA and Oolio's surface targets (POS, kiosk, KDS, back office, online) in three passes reported separately: automated (axe-core rules, contrast on rendered colours), assisted (keyboard-only run of every task, focus not obscured, names and roles from the accessibility tree, target sizes, a single-pointer alternative for every drag, reflow, errors linked to fields) and the human-required list (real screen reader, cognitive load).
catalogue.lede: Three passes, reported separately, so nobody mistakes an automated pass for conformance. Automated tools catch only part of the issues; keyboard, focus and assistive-technology checks catch the rest. The floor is **WCAG 2.2 AA**, one version ahead of the generic plugin's 2.1, and 2.2's new criteria bite Oolio directly: every drag in a menu builder needs a single-pointer alternative (2.5.7), and sticky control bars and drawers must not hide the focused field (2.4.11).
excludes: For a mockup with no build (design-council-review, or design:accessibility-review, which targets WCAG 2.1) or design-system checks (design-conformance)

catalogue.title: Persona UAT
catalogue.blurb: Run synthetic users through a live build, in character and under real constraints, before real people see it. Picks the test persona cards the epic touches (the literal-reading cafe owner, the Bepoz pub manager, the 12-venue ops lead, the online-first operator, the new casual, the chef at the pass, the fat finger at 8pm), writes a no-briefing task script (create, structure, populate, design, modify, recover, publish), runs each task in the browser as that persona, and produces a per-persona, per-task scorecard with what decided it. A pre-filter for obvious friction, never UAT sign-off. Trigger on "persona UAT", "run the personas through it", "walk it as Mia and Dave", "usability test with personas", "synthetic UAT", "would a new user get this".
catalogue.summary: Run synthetic users through a live build, in character and under real constraints, before real people see it.
catalogue.lede: The PR-1095 usability session as a repeatable skill. Synthetic personas walked the menu builder and found the problems the external session later confirmed: users could not tell what page they were on, what an edit would change, or whether anything was live. That is the job: clear the obvious friction cheaply so real sessions spend their time on the deep problems.
excludes: For real-user sessions (uat-session-kit) or for opinion on a mockup or decision (operator-council-review)

catalogue.title: UAT Session Kit
catalogue.blurb: Both ends of real-user UAT, the part that actually validates. Before: recruit criteria (personas, segments, pilot venues), the no-briefing task script, the facilitator and observer sheet, and the measures (task success, time on task, Single Ease Question, SUS). After: ingests Granola transcripts and notes, keys each source, de-dupes across sessions and against the synthetic run, themes it through defect-writer, and scores which real findings persona-uat predicted. Trigger on "plan the UAT sessions", "set up user testing", "pilot sessions for <release>", "write the observer sheet", "consolidate the UAT", "process the user testing transcripts", "how did synthetic UAT compare".
catalogue.summary: Both ends of real-user UAT, the part that actually validates.
catalogue.lede: Real-user UAT is the part of the family that validates; everything synthetic is a filter in front of it. This skill makes real sessions cheaper to run and faster to act on, and it measures whether the synthetic filter is earning its place.
excludes: For AI-only persona runs (persona-uat) or interview research on a problem space (design:user-research, synthesize-research)

catalogue.title: Code QA
catalogue.blurb: Read-only test intelligence: reads the repo and PR diff, never writes. Maps each acceptance criterion to the unit and integration tests that cover it, lists ACs with no test, rates risky changes by blast radius (shared helpers, resolvers, the POS gateway, pricing), proposes the missing tests as Given/When/Then for engineers to own, drafts Playwright specs as suggestions, and points the browser skills at regression risk. After an incident, proposes the regression test that would have caught it. Trigger on "what's the test coverage on this", "which ACs have no tests", "what does this PR touch", "blast radius of <PR>", "what tests are missing", "propose tests for <story>", "what test would have caught <incident>".
catalogue.summary: Read-only test intelligence: reads the repo and PR diff, never writes.
catalogue.lede: Push checks down the pyramid. Browser tests are slow and brittle; anything a unit or integration test can catch should be caught there, by engineers, in the repo. This skill makes sure the right tests get written, and tells the browser skills where to look, without ever touching the code.
excludes: For running tests in the browser (functional-qa)
General code review (engineering:code-review) or a general test strategy (engineering:testing-strategy)

catalogue.title: Resilience QA
catalogue.blurb: Test whether a build survives a real service, the Q4 question. Times key interactions against the Doherty threshold (about 400 ms for anything an operator waits on), runs against scale fixtures (thousands of products, many price lists times variants, a 40-venue group), simulates network loss and recovery mid-save and mid-publish, tests concurrent edits by two managers, and for POS-side work checks offline mode, the offline-versus-no-network states and sync-back. Trigger on "will it survive Friday night", "performance check", "is it fast enough", "what happens if the network drops", "test offline mode", "concurrent edits", "does it scale to a big group", "resilience test".
catalogue.summary: Test whether a build survives a real service, the Q4 question.
catalogue.lede: If a system fails under real operational pressure, it is not acceptable. The other specialists test the build on a quiet afternoon with a small catalogue and a good connection. This one tests it the way a venue uses it: at scale, under time pressure, with the network misbehaving and two people editing at once.
excludes: For infrastructure load testing or security testing (engineering and the security lead own those) or for edge cases at normal load (exploratory-qa)

catalogue.title: Defect Writer
catalogue.blurb: The single place QA findings are written, merged and routed, and the only writer of an epic's QA Review page. Takes findings from any QA skill, a tester, a UAT session or a pasted list, enforces no-oracle-no-defect, de-dupes across sources and open Jira, sets type, severity and confidence, then routes by stage. Before merge a failed AC reworks its story (drafted comment to the engineer and a transition back, no new ticket); after merge it drafts themed Bugs or Improvements. QA never creates Stories. All writes held for approval. Trigger on "write these up", "consolidate these findings", "turn this into tickets", "send it back for rework", "theme these UAT findings", "update the QA Review page", or a pasted list of test issues.
catalogue.summary: The single place QA findings are written, merged and routed, and the only writer of an epic's QA Review page.
catalogue.lede: Every QA skill reports through this one, so findings from six specialists, a human tester and a real UAT session land in one shape, with one severity scale, routed the way the team actually works. Engine and wrapper: the specialists find; this skill writes, merges, routes, and keeps the epic's one QA Review page.

catalogue.blurb: Turn an Oolio Jira release version into the full comms set, written in Oolio's house voice and verified against what actually shipped. Produces a Teams message for the business, customer page copy for HubSpot, an internal Confluence release page in the product's own space, a short Slack version, and a filed record in the brain.

catalogue.title: Metrics Review
catalogue.blurb: Run a product metrics review against real data — post-launch validation of a PRD's success metrics, or a recurring weekly/monthly product review — producing a scorecard with targets, actuals, trends, verdicts, and actions.
catalogue.summary: Run a product metrics review against real data — post-launch validation of a PRD's success metrics, or a recurring weekly/monthly product review — producing a scorecard with targets, actuals, trends, verdicts, and actions.
catalogue.lede: Close the loop the toolkit opens: the PRD promised success metrics, the council endorsed them, the feature shipped. This skill checks whether reality agrees, and turns the numbers into a scorecard with verdicts and actions. It also runs as a recurring review over a product area's standing metrics.

stages.name: Front Door
stages.purpose: You know you want help and not which kind. Say what you are facing and get pointed at the right skill, or hand over the whole muddle and let it be driven to something finished.

stages.name: Signals
stages.purpose: What the market, our lost deals and our own customers are telling us, gathered before anyone forms an opinion about it. Everything here ends up as cited evidence on the backlog rather than as a view.

stages.name: Brain
stages.purpose: The vault where findings accumulate, so what the team learns compounds instead of restarting every quarter. Read from it before researching something we may already know.

stages.name: Intake
stages.purpose: The gate between raw signal and the backlog. Most signal belongs on an idea that already exists, so the first job here is not creating one.

stages.name: Discovery
stages.purpose: The question is genuinely open. Research it properly with sources you can cite, or chart it as a map of decisions when it is too big to settle in one session.

stages.name: Grooming
stages.purpose: The idea exists but is not yet fit to be read, prioritised or decided. Bring it up to the house standard so the next person does not have to ask what it means.

stages.name: Definition
stages.purpose: Write down what we are actually doing, then attack it until it holds. The document is the deliverable; the argument is how it earns its place.

stages.name: Orchestration
stages.purpose: Run a whole chain rather than a single step, with a human sign-off at every point that counts. Reach for these when you want the loop, not one move in it.

stages.name: Council
stages.purpose: Four panels chosen to disagree with each other: the operators who have to live with it, the designers who judge whether it is any good, the leadership who fund it, and Roy.

stages.name: Steering
stages.purpose: Everything a roadmap review needs in order to decide, rather than to spend the hour asking for context.

stages.name: Delivery
stages.purpose: The work is committed and now lives in Jira. Keep it readable for everyone who was not in the room when it was decided.

stages.name: Quality
stages.purpose: It is built. Find out whether it is what we said, what we designed, usable by everyone and fit for a Friday night, before a customer does. A person makes the ship call, and only what was verified goes to market.

stages.name: GTM
stages.purpose: The product is real. Give the teams who sell it, support it and onboard customers onto it something they can use on Monday morning.

stages.name: Measure
stages.purpose: Close the loop the PRD opened. Find out whether we were right, and say so plainly on the occasions we were not.

map.title: Oolio Product OS
map.subtitle: THE PRODUCT OPERATING SYSTEM · SIGNAL → SHIPPED → LEARN

nodes.label: PM Compass
nodes.desc: The front door and router for the oolio-pm skills. Trigger when someone asks "which skill should I use", "where do I start", "what can these skills do", "what have you got for X", "help me choose", "I'm new to this", or describes a product-management task without naming a skill and the right one isn't obvious. Also trigger for "show me the pipeline" or "how do these skills fit together". Reads the situation, names the one skill (or short chain) that fits, and starts it on request. Do NOT trigger when the user already named a specific skill or their phrasing clearly matches one skill's own triggers — route straight there instead.

nodes.label: Drive
nodes.desc: Convert the user's most recent unstructured, rambling, or voice-dictated request into a clear execution contract, then plan, perform, review, and verify the work using whatever capabilities are available (files, connectors, web research, and document, spreadsheet, and presentation tools). Use whenever the user has rambled through an idea, given conflicting or half-formed instructions, described an outcome without a proper brief, referred loosely to "the deck" or "the report" or "the latest file", or wants Claude to take ownership and drive a task to a finished result rather than just discuss it. Invoke manually with /drive. Trigger automatically when a message reads as raw thinking aimed at a real outcome and the right move is to do the work, not to write back a tidier version of the request.

nodes.label: Competitor Watch
nodes.desc: Run Oolio's competitor intelligence: maintain one living dossier per competitor in the Brain, sweep the watchlist weekly and report only the deltas, deep-dive a competitor's reviews and communities for weaknesses, and build Fact-Impact-Act battlecards. Trigger when the user says "run the sweep", "competitor sweep", "watch the competition", "what's changed in the market", "update the <name> dossier", "deep-dive <competitor>", "build a battlecard for <competitor>", "what are <competitor>'s weaknesses", "what are competitors marketing", "check their campaigns/socials", "is <claim> real or marketing", or asks what a rival is doing, shipping, pricing, or hiring. Routes product-gap findings to `feedback-to-idea` and idea evidence to `signal-radar`. Do NOT trigger for validating a specific JPD idea (use signal-radar), a general research briefing (use storm-research), or win/loss deal analysis (use win-loss).

nodes.label: Win / Loss
nodes.desc: Mine HubSpot closed-lost and churn data for the real reasons Oolio wins and loses, monthly. Treats rep-entered loss reasons as hypotheses (buyer research shows they are wrong more often than right) and cross-examines deal metadata instead. Codes every loss on four drivers (product fit, sales experience, pricing/packaging, competitive), aggregates patterns by segment and competitor, routes product gaps to `feedback-to-idea`, competitor patterns to the `competitor-watch` dossiers, and drafts interview guides for the human follow-up calls. Trigger when the user says "run win/loss", "why are we losing deals", "mine closed-lost", "what's the win/loss picture this month/quarter", "who are we losing to", or asks why a segment or competitor keeps beating us. Do NOT trigger for a single deal post-mortem chat (just discuss it), competitor web research (use competitor-watch), or general idea validation (use signal-radar).

nodes.label: Signal Radar
nodes.desc: Synthesise HubSpot, web, and social signal (via Apify) into evidence for JPD ideas, and scan for gaps between market demand and the backlog. Two modes: idea mode (a JPD key: gathers evidence, attaches it as native Insights) and gap-scan mode (no key: scans the backlog for what the market wants and we do not cover, handing candidates to `feedback-to-idea`). Findings land in the Brain. Trigger when the user says "run signal radar", "sync the brain", "what's the market saying about X", "validate this idea with real signal", "find gaps in the backlog / roadmap", "what are we missing", or "scan HubSpot and social for signal". Do NOT trigger for already-found evidence (use `add-insight`), pasted feedback (use `feedback-to-idea`), the full VPC loop (use `jpd-loop`), a deep-dive with no backlog tie-in (use `storm-research`), competitor dossiers or battlecards (use `competitor-watch`), or closed-lost deals (use `win-loss`).

nodes.label: Add Insight
nodes.desc: Attach a single piece of evidence to the JPD backlog as native Insights, on one idea or several. Trigger when the user hands over one finding — a URL, an article, a HubSpot ticket or deal, a quote, a stat, a screenshot description, something spotted mid-session — and says "attach this as an insight", "add this to OHSI-X (and OHSI-Y)", "this supports that idea about X", "where does this belong on the backlog", "file this against the relevant ideas", or "make this an insight". Works evidence-first: given targets it attaches after a fit check; given none it sweeps the backlog for every idea the evidence genuinely supports and proposes the mapping. Do NOT trigger for gathering evidence about an idea or scanning for gaps (use `signal-radar`), for raw customer feedback that may need a new idea (use `feedback-to-idea`), or for the full grooming loop (use `jpd-loop`).

nodes.label: HubSpot Sweep
nodes.desc: The daily HubSpot sweep: pull the last day's CRM signal, match it against the JPD backlog, and attach what fits as native Insights, so customer need reaches discovery without anyone having to read the support queue. Runs on a schedule or on demand. Trigger when the user says "run the hubspot sweep", "the daily hubspot check", "what's new in hubspot", "check hubspot for insights", "any new signal from support", "daily CRM sweep", or when a scheduled daily run fires. Covers feature and change requests, cancellations, offboarding, and at-risk accounts across the support pipelines. Do NOT trigger for one piece of evidence already in hand (use `add-insight`), for gathering evidence on a single named idea or a full backlog gap scan (use `signal-radar`), for raw pasted feedback (use `feedback-to-idea`), for closed-lost deal analysis (use `win-loss`), or for the full grooming loop (use `jpd-loop`).

nodes.label: Wiki Ingest
nodes.desc: Ingest a source into the my_brain vault — read it, distill it, and integrate it across the owning domain's Capability, Concept, Synthesis and Overview pages while writing a provenance-carrying source summary and updating the domain catalogue and log. Trigger when the user drops a file in a domain's Sources/ folder and says "ingest this", "add this to the Brain", "file this in the vault", or names a source to process. Routes to the correct Product Domain or the cross-cutting Market area, and handles competitor content via the canonical-in-Market rule. Do NOT trigger to answer a question (use wiki-query), to health-check the vault (use wiki-lint), or to stand up a new domain (use wiki-new).

nodes.desc: Answer a question against the my_brain vault with citations to its pages, reading the domain README and Overview first to locate the right pages, then offering to file durable answers back as a synthesis so explorations compound. Trigger when the user asks something to be answered from the Brain, the vault, or the wiki — "ask the Brain…", "what does the vault say about…", "query the Brain", "according to the Brain…", "what do we know about a competitor, feature, or metric" — or asks an Oolio product, competitor, or capability question while working in the vault. Do NOT trigger to ingest a new source (use wiki-ingest), to health-check the vault (use wiki-lint), or to stand up a new domain (use wiki-new).

nodes.label: Wiki Lint
nodes.desc: Health-check the my_brain vault for contradictions, stale claims, orphan pages, missing cross-references, missing or wrong frontmatter (including missing class or a past review date), competitor-pattern violations, and data gaps. Trigger when the user says "lint", "lint the Brain", "lint Insights", "health-check the vault", "audit the Brain", or "check the vault for issues". Proposes fixes and new questions to investigate, changes only on approval, and logs the pass. Do NOT trigger for a quick overview snapshot (use wiki-status), to ingest a source (use wiki-ingest), or to answer a question (use wiki-query).

nodes.desc: Produce a status snapshot of the my_brain vault — per-domain page counts by type, recent activity from the logs and git, stub domains, orphans, pages missing class or past their review date, and gaps worth filling. Trigger when the user says "Brain status", "vault status", "what's in the Brain", "show me the state of the vault", "what's been ingested lately", or wants an at-a-glance overview before deciding what to work on. Read-only. Do NOT trigger for a deep correctness pass (use wiki-lint), to ingest a source (use wiki-ingest), or to answer a question (use wiki-query).

Trigger when the user says "add a new domain", "create a Payments domain", "stand up a new wiki", "add a domain to the Brain", or names a capability area they want tracked separately. Confirms scope and boundaries before any material lands, and creates no empty scaffolding. Do NOT trigger to ingest a source into an existing domain (use wiki-ingest), to answer a question (use wiki-query), or to health-check the vault (use wiki-lint).

nodes.label: Push to Brain
nodes.note: session → the note that owns it
nodes.desc: Push the durable knowledge from the current conversation into the my_brain vault by changing what the Brain already holds. Appends to an existing section, edits outdated wording, updates a status or a decision, inserts a section into the right existing note, and creates a new note only when no home exists. Trigger ONLY on an explicit invocation at the end of a working session, such as "/push-to-brain", "push this to the brain", "push to brain", "save this session to the brain", or "update the brain with what we decided". nodes.desc: Turn raw customer, support, or sales signal into a Jira Product Discovery idea, or attach the signal to an existing idea, de-duped against the whole backlog. Trigger PROACTIVELY when the user pastes customer feedback, a support trend, a Slack thread, a HubSpot ticket or deal note, a churn reason, or a feature request and says "raise this as an idea", "get this into JPD", "log this feedback", "is this already on the backlog", or "turn this into an idea". Also trigger when the user asks to sweep a channel or ticket queue for product signal. Do NOT trigger for grooming an existing idea (use jpd-idea-groomer), for running the full loop (use jpd-loop), or for general feedback summarisation with no JPD intent.

nodes.label: Storm Research
nodes.desc: Use when someone asks to run Storm Research, use the storm-research skill, run the STORM method on a topic, says "storm research this" / "storm report on X" / "give me a STORM briefing on X", or wants a multi-perspective, citation-verified research briefing delivered as a clean HTML report and, optionally, a Confluence page. Also the research engine the Virtual Product Council calls before its panels argue. Runs a 4-phase pipeline: five expert lenses (Practitioner, Academic, Skeptic, Economist, Historian) -> contradiction map -> synthesized HTML report -> adversarial peer review + primary-source verification, then publishes. Best where multiple viewpoints and fact-checked claims matter; overkill for a simple factual lookup.

nodes.label: Discovery Wayfinder
nodes.desc: Chart a product discovery theme too big for one session ("AI ordering strategy", "what does labour cost control mean for us") as a shared map of decision tickets in Jira, then work the map one decision at a time until the way is clear. nodes.label: JPD Title Standard

nodes.label: Write PRD

nodes.label: Grill Me

nodes.label: Story Mockups

nodes.label: JPD Loop

nodes.label: Convene VPC
nodes.desc: Convene the Oolio Virtual Product Council to pressure-test a product decision, design, requirement, spec, PRD, or piece of research. nodes.label: Operator Council
nodes.desc: Test a decision against the Oolio Operator Council, the hospitality user personas (the UAT panel). nodes.label: Design Council

nodes.label: Leadership Sub-cttee

nodes.label: Behavioural Alchemist

nodes.label: Steering Pack

nodes.label: Jira Epic Groomer
nodes.desc: Groom or backfill the description on a Jira epic so it follows Oolio's standard What/Why/Who pattern. Trigger PROACTIVELY whenever the user references a Jira epic key (`OR-XXXX`, `EDU-XXXX`, `IDEA-XXXX` flagged as Epic, etc.) and asks to "describe", "groom", "polish", "backfill", "tidy up", "sharpen", "rewrite", or "write a description for" the epic. nodes.label: Jira Epic Titler
nodes.desc: Suggest a stronger Oolio Jira epic title using the `[Capability] for [Outcome]` standard. nodes.label: GTM Handover

Don't trigger for campaign material, use gtm-marketing. Don't trigger for a single tagline edit, edit the file directly.

nodes.label: GTM Playbooks
nodes.desc: Build the three internal-facing GTM playbooks for a single Oolio product. Sales (discovery, demo, objections, pricing, close), Account Management (adoption signals, expansion, renewal, at-risk, QBR), and Onboarding (configuration, migration, training, go-live, first-week). Trigger PROACTIVELY when the user asks to "build the GTM playbooks for [product]", "do the sales playbook", "do the AM playbook", "do the onboarding playbook", "draft the playbooks for [product]", "build the rep enablement", or any combination of the three. nodes.label: GTM Marketing

Don't trigger for sales / AM / onboarding playbooks, use gtm-playbooks. Reads pack_content.json produced by gtm-handover and refuses to run if that file is missing.

nodes.label: Release Notes
nodes.desc: Turn an Oolio Jira release version into the full comms set, written in Oolio's house voice and verified against what actually shipped. Produces a Teams message for the business, customer page copy for HubSpot, an internal Confluence release page in the product's own space, a short Slack version, and a filed record in the brain. Trigger when the user hands over a Jira version URL or id (a /projects/<KEY>/versions/<id> link, or "release notes for 23878"), or says "write the release notes", "do the release comms", "we shipped this yesterday", or pastes a release report. Also handles a product notice, where a capability is withdrawn, paused or changed outside a release. Do NOT trigger for a GTM launch pack (gtm-handover), a stakeholder update (product-management:stakeholder-update), or writing up defects (defect-writer).

nodes.label: Metrics Review
nodes.desc: Run a product metrics review against real data — post-launch validation of a PRD's success metrics, or a recurring weekly/monthly product review — producing a scorecard with targets, actuals, trends, verdicts, and actions. Trigger PROACTIVELY when the user says "metrics review", "how is [feature] performing", "did [launch] work", "check the success metrics", "weekly product review", "validate the launch", or names a shipped PRD/feature and asks whether it met its numbers. Uses the connected PostHog MCP where available, and PRD success metrics as the target source. Do NOT trigger for ad-hoc SQL help or building a dashboard (use the data skills), or for market research (storm-research).

nodes.label: QA Mission
nodes.desc: The quality gate and orchestrator of the QA family, for releases what convene-vpc is for decisions. Takes an epic, fix version, PR preview or flag, runs test-basis and stops on high-consequence conflicts; picks Smoke, Standard or Full by risk; convenes the specialists that tier needs (functional, exploratory, design, accessibility, persona UAT, code, resilience, councils in built mode); merges through defect-writer; verifies independently; recommends Ship, Ship with known issues or Hold; and hands GTM only verified claims and metrics-review a measurable launch. Learn mode turns escapes into method fixes. Trigger on "QA this release", "is it ready to ship", "run QA on <epic>", "release verdict", "quality gate", "what did QA miss". Do NOT trigger for one specialist pass (call that skill), a decision, PRD or mockup (convene-vpc), or a deploy checklist (engineering:deploy-checklist).

nodes.label: Test Basis
nodes.desc: Build the Test Basis for a release, epic or PR before anyone tests it. Gathers every source that says what the build should be (PRD, stories and ACs, decisions, meetings, Figma, the diff), finds where they disagree, flags untestable ACs with Given/When/Then rewrites, checks every success metric can be measured, rates each flow Frequency × Consequence, and maps the blast radius. Trigger on "build the test basis", "what should we test", "is this spec testable", "line up the sources", "are the sources consistent", "is this measurable", "risk map for <release>", or a release key with "before we test". The first step of every qa-mission run. Never resolves a conflict; dates it and hands it to a person. Do NOT trigger to run tests (functional-qa, exploratory-qa), to grill the PRD (grill-my-prd), a general test strategy (engineering:testing-strategy), or the full QA run (qa-mission).

nodes.label: Functional QA
nodes.desc: Run a release's acceptance criteria as concrete examples against the live build, in the browser, by role and name, and confirm the analytics events its success metrics need actually fire. Pass, Fail or Blocked per AC with evidence, at least one negative case each, technique chosen by the rule's shape (boundaries, decision tables, state transitions, pairwise). Also re-runs the product area's regression pack. Trigger on "test the ACs", "does it do what the story says", "functional test <story/epic/PR>", "run the regression pack", "check the events fire", "is it instrumented", "verify this fix". Reports through defect-writer, so a failed AC before merge sends the story back for rework. Do NOT trigger for off-script exploration (exploratory-qa), design or accessibility checks (design-conformance, accessibility-audit), or the full release run (qa-mission).

nodes.label: Exploratory QA
nodes.desc: Run chartered, timeboxed exploratory testing sessions against a live build to find what breaks off the happy path, the defects nobody wrote an AC for. Charters come from the risk map, the hospitality conditions library (midnight trading days, two managers in two tabs, back button mid-publish, empty venues, big catalogues) and past failures; SFDPOT checks coverage and HICCUPPS recognises problems. Session notes are the evidence. Trigger on "explore this", "try to break it", "exploratory test", "what happens off the happy path", "edge cases on <feature>", "run some charters", "bug bash". Reports through defect-writer. Do NOT trigger for scripted AC checks (functional-qa), synthetic users in character (persona-uat), load, network loss or scale (resilience-qa), or the full release run (qa-mission).

nodes.label: Design Conformance
nodes.desc: Check that the built screen is what was designed, in the system's own components. Compares the live build, in order, against the Figma frame for the work, the component reference (is this the real ControlBar or a lookalike, are all states present, does the Select follow its rules), the pattern library (navigation in the shell, drawers versus modals, save versus publish, destructive actions, empty and error states), the design tokens, and the glossary. Tags every deviation deliberate, drift or system gap, so drift goes to engineering and gaps go to Design. Trigger on "does the build match the design", "check it against Figma", "design QA", "is this our component", "pass it through design", "check the copy against the glossary". Do NOT trigger to judge whether the design itself is good (design-council-review, built mode) or for WCAG checks (accessibility-audit).

nodes.label: Accessibility Audit
nodes.desc: Audit a live build against WCAG 2.2 AA and Oolio's surface targets (POS, kiosk, KDS, back office, online) in three passes reported separately: automated (axe-core rules, contrast on rendered colours), assisted (keyboard-only run of every task, focus not obscured, names and roles from the accessibility tree, target sizes, a single-pointer alternative for every drag, reflow, errors linked to fields) and the human-required list (real screen reader, cognitive load). Produces findings against the success criterion and a VPAT-shaped summary. Trigger on "accessibility audit", "is this accessible", "WCAG check", "keyboard test this", "check contrast", "can everyone use it", "we need an ACR or VPAT". Do NOT trigger for a mockup with no build (design-council-review, or design:accessibility-review, which targets WCAG 2.1) or design-system checks (design-conformance).

nodes.label: Persona UAT
nodes.desc: Run synthetic users through a live build, in character and under real constraints, before real people see it. Picks the test persona cards the epic touches (the literal-reading cafe owner, the Bepoz pub manager, the 12-venue ops lead, the online-first operator, the new casual, the chef at the pass, the fat finger at 8pm), writes a no-briefing task script (create, structure, populate, design, modify, recover, publish), runs each task in the browser as that persona, and produces a per-persona, per-task scorecard with what decided it. A pre-filter for obvious friction, never UAT sign-off. Trigger on "persona UAT", "run the personas through it", "walk it as Mia and Dave", "usability test with personas", "synthetic UAT", "would a new user get this". Do NOT trigger for real-user sessions (uat-session-kit) or for opinion on a mockup or decision (operator-council-review).

nodes.label: UAT Session Kit
nodes.desc: Both ends of real-user UAT, the part that actually validates. Before: recruit criteria (personas, segments, pilot venues), the no-briefing task script, the facilitator and observer sheet, and the measures (task success, time on task, Single Ease Question, SUS). After: ingests Granola transcripts and notes, keys each source, de-dupes across sessions and against the synthetic run, themes it through defect-writer, and scores which real findings persona-uat predicted. Trigger on "plan the UAT sessions", "set up user testing", "pilot sessions for <release>", "write the observer sheet", "consolidate the UAT", "process the user testing transcripts", "how did synthetic UAT compare". Do NOT trigger for AI-only persona runs (persona-uat) or interview research on a problem space (design:user-research, synthesize-research).

nodes.label: Code QA
nodes.desc: Read-only test intelligence: reads the repo and PR diff, never writes. Maps each acceptance criterion to the unit and integration tests that cover it, lists ACs with no test, rates risky changes by blast radius (shared helpers, resolvers, the POS gateway, pricing), proposes the missing tests as Given/When/Then for engineers to own, drafts Playwright specs as suggestions, and points the browser skills at regression risk. After an incident, proposes the regression test that would have caught it. Trigger on "what's the test coverage on this", "which ACs have no tests", "what does this PR touch", "blast radius of <PR>", "what tests are missing", "propose tests for <story>", "what test would have caught <incident>". Do NOT trigger for running tests in the browser (functional-qa), general code review (engineering:code-review) or a general test strategy (engineering:testing-strategy).

nodes.label: Resilience QA
nodes.desc: Test whether a build survives a real service, the Q4 question. Times key interactions against the Doherty threshold (about 400 ms for anything an operator waits on), runs against scale fixtures (thousands of products, many price lists times variants, a 40-venue group), simulates network loss and recovery mid-save and mid-publish, tests concurrent edits by two managers, and for POS-side work checks offline mode, the offline-versus-no-network states and sync-back. Trigger on "will it survive Friday night", "performance check", "is it fast enough", "what happens if the network drops", "test offline mode", "concurrent edits", "does it scale to a big group", "resilience test". Do NOT trigger for infrastructure load testing or security testing (engineering and the security lead own those) or for edge cases at normal load (exploratory-qa).

nodes.label: Defect Writer
nodes.desc: The single place QA findings are written, merged and routed, and the only writer of an epic's QA Review page. Takes findings from any QA skill, a tester, a UAT session or a pasted list, enforces no-oracle-no-defect, de-dupes across sources and open Jira, sets type, severity and confidence, then routes by stage. Before merge a failed AC reworks its story (drafted comment to the engineer and a transition back, no new ticket); after merge it drafts themed Bugs or Improvements. QA never creates Stories. All writes held for approval. Trigger on "write these up", "consolidate these findings", "turn this into tickets", "send it back for rework", "theme these UAT findings", "update the QA Review page", or a pasted list of test issues. Do NOT trigger for raw customer feedback (feedback-to-idea), a single incident (customer-escalation), or to run testing (qa-mission).

loops.label: EVERY RUN COMPOUNDS IN THE BRAIN

flows.name: Signal → Shipped → Learn
path: A rival ships. The weekly sweep catches the delta and flags the gap.
The gap becomes a cited JPD idea, de-duped against the whole backlog.
It lands natively in Jira with its evidence attached.
Groomed to Oolio's field standard: problem, hypothesis, metrics, all fields.
The groomed idea becomes a high-level PRD.
Niel is interviewed one question at a time until the decision tree resolves.
The Virtual Product Council is chaired over the PRD.
Hospitality personas test it against real venue reality.
The chair records a validated decision on the log.
The decision becomes a delivery epic in the What/Why/Who pattern.
One-pager, deck and pack_content.json: the launch source of truth.
Sales, AM and onboarding playbooks built from the pack.
Six launch artifacts, ready to ship.
After launch, did it hit its success metrics?
Target vs actual. The verdict feeds the next idea.

flows.name: JPD Loop — Idea to Decision
path: Groomed and de-duped against the whole backlog first.
The orchestrator picks it up and runs it end to end.
Human sign-off, then moved to Decision.

flows.name: PRD → Launch
path: Pressure-tested with Niel until decisions are locked.

flows.name: Evidence Engine
path: Closed-lost mined from HubSpot for loss drivers.
All of it converges into ideas.

flows.name: The Brain Compounds
path: A sweep turns up something worth keeping.
The source is read, distilled, and integrated with its provenance.
It lands in my_brain, the vault the whole team reads.
Next time someone asks, the answer comes back cited, not from zero.
What the vault knows becomes a shaped idea.

flows.name: Ship & Learn Loop
path: Measured against its targets, and the scorecard written down.
A breached metric becomes the next idea. The loop closes.
Back at the top of the funnel, with evidence this time.

flows.name: Spec → Tested → Proven
path: The stories and their acceptance criteria are built.
PRD, stories, decisions, Figma and code lined up. Conflicts go to a person before anyone tests.
The tier is set by risk and the specialists run in parallel.
Synthetic users walk it in character and predict where real ones will stall.
A failed AC before merge reworks the story. After merge, themed Bugs and Improvements.
One page per epic: what was tested, by whom, when, and the result.
The pack claims only what QA verified, and says the known issues plainly.
The promised metrics, proven measurable before launch, checked against reality.

systems.title: How the data moves
systems.subtitle: SIGNAL IN · THE OS · SYSTEMS OF RECORD · THE VAULT UNDERNEATH

intro.kicker: Thirteen systems. One direction of travel.
lede: Signal arrives from wherever it lives: a meeting, a deal, a rival's pricing page, a Slack thread nobody else read. The Product OS is what reads it, and the systems of record are where it lands as work.

Nothing here talks to anything else directly. Every arrow passes through the middle, which is the whole point: one place that knows the standard, so the same thing does not get written four different ways in four different tools.
intro.note: Cadence and scope come from the Brain's ingestion contract, not from memory. Click a system to see what we read from it and what we write back.

systems.label: Granola
reads: Every meeting transcript, all folders
systems.detail: A meeting earns a page in the vault only if it produced a decision, a material action, or a knowledge signal. Everything else becomes one line in that month's log, carrying its Granola id. Granola stays the full record; the vault keeps the distillate.

systems.label: Slack
reads: #product-mgmt and #core-pos
Anything that mentions Niel
Threads he took part in since the last run
systems.detail: Distil only. Full message bodies never leave Slack and never land in the vault, which keeps a channel's noise out of the knowledge layer while its signal still gets through.

systems.label: Microsoft 365
reads: Teams mentions and threads
Unread and flagged mail addressed to Niel
Today's calendar, to frame the morning brief
SharePoint strategy and QBR material, on demand
systems.detail: What gets extracted is the ask, the decision, the commitment. Not the mail. An inbox copied into a vault is still an inbox.

systems.label: HubSpot
reads: Closed-lost deals and their loss reasons
Support tickets and their trends
Deal notes behind a specific claim
systems.detail: Deliberately not in the nightly sweep. Commercial data is pulled when a question needs it and cited when it is used, rather than mirrored wholesale into a second place it can go stale.

systems.label: Apify
reads: Competitor sites, pricing and changelogs
Review sites and app store ratings
Operator communities and social
systems.detail: The outside world does not have an API, so Apify is how we read it. Actors are pinned per source, and every finding carries the URL it came from, because an uncited competitor claim is a rumour.

systems.label: The open web
reads: Competitors named in the Market wiki
Material moves only: funding, launches, pricing, M&A
systems.detail: Scoped to the competitors we already track, and to moves that would change a decision. A general news feed would be noise wearing a research badge.

systems.label: PostHog
reads: Events and funnels behind a PRD's success metrics
Adoption and retention after a launch
systems.detail: The only system on this map that can tell us we were wrong. Its numbers are read against targets a PRD committed to before launch, so the verdict is not chosen after the fact.

systems.label: Figma
reads: Frames, flows and prototypes handed to the Design Council
systems.detail: Read as evidence, not as a source of truth. A design enters the map when someone asks the council to test it, and leaves as a verdict on the decision record.

systems.label: The Product OS
reads: Everything on the left, through MCP connectors
writes: Everything on the right, through the same connectors
systems.detail: Not a system we bought. It is the plugin, installed by real people in Cowork, that knows the house standard and applies it the same way every time. Every arrow on this page passes through here, which is what stops thirteen tools becoming thirteen conventions.

systems.label: Jira Product Discovery
reads: The whole idea backlog, for de-duplication
Existing insights already attached to an idea
writes: New ideas, de-duped against the backlog first
The full field standard: pillar, theme, size, persona, commitment
systems.detail: Where a signal stops being a message and becomes a candidate. Evidence attaches natively rather than being pasted into a description, so an idea's case can be read without reading the thread it came from.

systems.label: Jira
reads: Existing issues, before anything is created
Status changes and due-soon items, for the brief
writes: Groomed epics in the What / Why / Who pattern
Titles held to the capability-for-outcome standard
systems.detail: Search, link, check, validate, and only create if it is genuinely needed. Every write is amber: a person approves it. The fastest way to ruin a backlog is to let something tireless write to it.

systems.label: Confluence
reads: Existing PRDs and decision records
Pages changed since the last run, in scope spaces
writes: PRDs, and the grill record that resolved them
systems.detail: The human-readable front door. A decision that only exists in a chat log gets relitigated in six weeks, so the council's verdict is written down where the next person will actually find it.

systems.label: GitHub
reads: Activity across the OS repo and the vault repo
writes: The Product OS itself, versioned by commit
systems.detail: Two repos: the plugin the team installs, and the vault it writes into. Both are versioned by commit rather than by a number someone has to remember to bump, which is why an edit reaches the team without a release.

systems.label: The Brain
reads: Whatever a question needs, answered with citations
systems.detail: The floor the whole thing stands on. Owned markdown, typed pages, supersession instead of deletion, and answers that come back with receipts. It is why the second time someone asks a question, the answer does not start from zero.

routes.name: A meeting becomes work
path: Someone says something that matters in a call nobody wrote up.
The nightly ingest reads the transcript and asks one question: did this produce a decision, an action, or something worth knowing?
If it did, it earns a page. The decision is typed and dated, the action becomes a checkbox, and both carry the meeting they came from.
Actions that turn out to be real work get picked up and routed.
It becomes a ticket, with a person approving the write. The thing said out loud in a call is now on a board.

routes.name: Customer signal reaches the backlog
path: A deal closes lost, or the same complaint arrives on the fourth ticket this month.
The signal is checked against the entire idea backlog before anything is created, because the fastest way to break a backlog is to fill it with the same idea five times.
It lands as an idea, or attaches to the one that already exists, with the evidence as a native insight rather than a pasted quote.
The finding is worth keeping beyond this one idea.
It joins what we already know about that domain, so the next person to ask starts further ahead.

routes.name: Watching the market
path: A rival changes their pricing page. The weekly sweep reads the site, the reviews and the communities around it.
The delta is what matters, not the snapshot. Only what changed since last time gets reported.
The competitor's dossier is updated in place, so there is one living page per rival instead of nine dated documents.
A change that opens a real gap gets routed forward.
The gap becomes a cited insight on the ideas it actually supports.
The sales team need it in a form they can use in a room.

routes.name: Idea to shipped
path: A groomed idea with a problem, a hypothesis and success metrics it has agreed to be judged on.
It becomes a PRD, gets pressure-tested question by question, and goes to the council for a verdict.
The PRD and the validated decision are published where the next person will find them.
The decision becomes delivery work, in the house pattern.
A groomed epic, and the launch pack that hangs off it.

routes.name: Did it actually work?
path: The feature has been live a month. The numbers exist whether or not anyone looks.
Actuals are read against the targets the PRD committed to before launch, so the bar cannot move after the result is known.
A scorecard: target, actual, trend, verdict. Including the verdicts nobody enjoys.
A breached metric is not a post-mortem, it is a signal.
It goes back in the top of the funnel as a new idea, with evidence this time.

routes.name: The nightly sweep
path: At 10pm, with nobody watching: Slack channels and mentions, Teams and Outlook, Jira movement, Confluence changes, GitHub activity, and every meeting of the day.
One run, one contract. Each source has a declared scope, and anything found outside it is proposed in the morning brief rather than quietly ingested.
What survives the promotion gate becomes pages. What does not becomes one line in a log, still findable, not cluttering the vault.
Committed and pushed automatically. By morning the brief is written, and the vault on every device is the same vault.

changelog.title: release-notes: one release, one record, four audiences (47 skills)
changelog.heading: 2026-10-06 – release-notes: one release, one record, four audiences (47 skills)
changelog.body:
A release was a Jira state change nobody outside the team noticed, and a comms effort that started from scratch each time. September 2026 produced four releases by hand (Products App mPOS and fixes, Insights saved and scheduled reports, Insights roles and permissions, the Ngara September update), and two of the three Jira ones were announced with items that had not actually shipped and the version not flipped. The method that caught that, written down in the Brain as the Release Launch Pattern, is now **release-notes**, the skill. It is the judgement and the voice; the plumbing (a morning sweep, fan-out on approval) stays out of it by design.

- **What it makes.** From one Jira version: a Teams message for the business, customer page copy for HubSpot, an internal Confluence release page in the product's own space, a short Slack version, and a filed record in the Brain. Same facts, four registers, never a copy and paste of each other. Also a product notice, for a capability withdrawn, paused or changed outside a release.
- **Status, never membership.** Every item in the version is classified from its status: `Released / GA` is shipped, `Prod-Green - Feature Flagged` is deployed but possibly invisible, everything else is not shipped. A not-shipped item is named as such in Teams and does not exist on the customer page. A flagged item is never announced as available.
- **The why is a person's.** The skill refuses to draft without one. If the user has not said why the release mattered, it asks one question offering the three shapes that have covered every release so far: a promise being broken, a gap forcing a workaround, a trade the customer should never have had to make.
- **The next two releases, always.** Taken from the project's unreleased versions in date order, each with its date and one operator sentence, flagged subject to change. The standard from 29 September.
- **The gate.** Assemble and draft, then stop. Nothing is posted, published or written back to Jira until a person approves. At most three go / no-go caveats in chat, each one a flag from the record.
- **Grounded on the real thing.** The worked example is the 28 September Insights release (OR version 23878), where Jira was clean and the verification pass still caught two incidents a screenshot showed as fixed and Jira showed otherwise. Two query gotchas found while building are now in the reference: `OR` is a JQL operator, so Insights' project key must be quoted, and the Insights Confluence space alias `in` is a CQL reserved word.
- **One correction to the brief.** The draft allowed an em dash in a Confluence page title "where Oolio's title standard requires it". The Confluence Naming Standard in the Brain says the opposite: the pipe is the only separator, and the em dash is banned outright. Titles follow `<YYYY-MM> <subject> | Release Note`. No em dash anywhere.
- **Eleven reference files.** Voice, method (with notice mode and the anti-patterns already caught), the Jira and Confluence queries, the release record schema, the verification checklist, the product map (Insights, Products App, Ngara: Jira project, Confluence space, Brain folder, slug pattern), worked examples, and one template per artefact. The notice example is a shape, not a precedent, and says so; the first real notice replaces it.
- **Where it sits.** GTM, after the ship call. `qa-mission` hands it verified claims only; it feeds `metrics-review` with what was announced. Not a launch pack (`gtm-handover`), not a stakeholder update, not defects.
- **Counts and catalogues.** 46 → **47**. Manifests, both READMEs, the catalogue, `pm-compass` routing, the strict no-em-dash lint, and the site map: a new plate in the GTM column.

changelog.title: story-mockups: from stories to screens people can argue with (46 skills)
changelog.heading: 2026-10-06 – story-mockups: from stories to screens people can argue with (46 skills)
changelog.body:
The gap between a groomed PRD and a design review was a blank Figma page. A PM with stories and acceptance criteria had nothing concrete to put in front of engineering until a designer found time, and the first design conversation happened on a document rather than a screen. On 6 October the scheduled reports stories (OR-2824 to OR-2827 under OR-1903) were mocked up by hand from the Oolio components in about a session: 13 frames, 4 sections, 51 annotations, 10 comments. **story-mockups** is that run written down as a skill.

- **What it makes.** One Figma Section per story, the primary screen plus every state the stories imply (empty, loading, could not load, confirmations, toasts, unsaved changes, no permission), a title block and a heading above every frame, native annotations in the five house categories, and every open question posted as a Figma comment through Claude in Chrome. Every acceptance criterion is on a frame or on a not-visualised list that ships with the report.
- **Components, not drawings.** Every element is the Office component in code, its UI Library twin, or a pattern already on the file; a local component is the last resort and is logged as a design-system gap. No raw primitive where a component exists, no hardcoded colour or size where a variable exists. The design system is re-read on every run from the design and backoffice repos and the library, because keys change when the library is republished and the patterns moved twice in September.
- **It is a mockup, and it says so.** A fast first pass for product and engineering to review and comment on, then the designer fine-tunes on the same page. Anything the sources cannot settle becomes a comment with a recommended answer, never a guess on the canvas. Dark mode is built light only and flagged, because the library's Dark tokens leave surfaces light.
- **Where it sits.** Definition, after `write-prd` and the stories: `design-council-review` judges the mockup, `design-conformance` later checks the build against it. The compass routes "mock this up" and "what would it look like" to it.
- **Four reference files** carry what the run learnt: how Office composes drawers, create, overlays, copy and status; the component map with the library keys and the three gaps to raise with Design (a SideDrawer twin, a Sticker colour variant, working Dark values); the Plugin API gotchas; and the annotation and comment house style, carried in the plugin so Cowork users without the `figma-annotate` skill get the same rules.
- **Defaults taken where the handoff left questions.** The skill keeps the name `story-mockups`; it always asks before adding the Figma link to the epic, like every other Jira write in the plugin; the default target is a page per epic inside the product's own Figma file; and the Design asks are drafted in the component map for Niel to raise.
- **Counts and catalogues.** 45 → **46**. Manifests, both READMEs, the catalogue, `pm-compass` routing, `write-prd`'s next step, and the site map: a new plate in the Definition column fed by the PRD, feeding the Design Council and design conformance.

changelog.title: One system, end to end: the paper edition of the site
changelog.heading: 2026-10-02 – One system, end to end: the paper edition of the site
changelog.body:
The first reprint of the day fixed the map and the library and quietened the inks, and it was still not one thing. A round button on one page, a square chip on another, a black keyline here, a halftone wash there, three faces that argued. The site now reads from one short set of decisions on every page, and the build fails when a page drifts from them.

- **Type.** Newsreader, regular weight, for the argument: page titles, section lines, the wordmark. Geist for everything a person reads or clicks. Geist Mono for every label, count and command. Mincho and Gothic, the classic pairing. Syne and Archivo are retired.
- **Shape.** Three radii, by role: 6px for a tag or a code span, 10px for every button, input, chip and selectable row, 14px for every card, panel, tile and drawer. No pills. A radius off the scale fails `npm --prefix site run check`.
- **The fold.** The origami idea, in eighteen pixels: a dog-ear on the top right corner of any surface that holds content, in the stock and the pink tint. The hero's findings sheet, the map's panel cards, the skill's Run it sheet, each changelog entry, the sign-in confirmation. One per surface, never on a control. It is the same mark on every page, and it is the only decoration.
- **One button, one label, one surface.** The black drum for the primary action, one per view; a lifted sheet with a firm edge for the secondary. The eyebrow above every title. The surface for every card.
- **Textures gone.** The halftone washes behind the hero, the dotted ground under the systems map, the overprint blend and the pulsing core are retired. Grain at eight per cent is the only texture, and the sheet is otherwise plain.
- **Every page, not the three big ones.** Sign-in, members, changelog, about, Flightdeck and the systems map were brought onto the same furniture, and the link preview card is set in the same serif on the same folded sheet.
- The brand documents say all of this in one place: [brand/README.md](brand/README.md) under "One system", [brand/typography.md](brand/typography.md), [brand/colour.md](brand/colour.md).

changelog.title: The site reprinted: a snake map, a skills library with a drawer, and muted inks from the Dictionary (45 skills)
changelog.heading: 2026-10-02 – The site reprinted: a snake map, a skills library with a drawer, and muted inks from the Dictionary (45 skills)
changelog.body:
The site had outgrown two of its own ideas. The map laid fourteen stages in one row and stacked each stage's skills in a column, which was legible at thirty skills and a strip of unreadable boxes at forty-five: a 13.5px label drawn at a third of its size is not a label. The skills page was forty-five cards that each opened a separate page. And the fluorescent press was loud in every corner at once. All three were audited and fixed in one pass, recorded in [docs/site-ux-audit-2026-10-02.md](docs/site-ux-audit-2026-10-02.md).

- **The map is a snake.** Stages one to seven run left to right along the top, the lifecycle turns, and eight to fourteen run back along the bottom. A crowded stage packs its skills into lanes, so every plate in a band is the same height and the canvas is roughly the shape of the screen. A strip of stage chips across the top zooms to any stage at any size; a plate does the same; a tile selects a skill, glides to it, and fills the panel with its summary, its connections and a link into the library. Far away, tiles show their label alone; close up, the note and the tool badge return. The panel always answers where you are: a flow's steps, a stage's purpose and skills, or a skill's card. Loops run through the channel between the bands. One bead travels one wire every couple of seconds, so the sheet reads as alive; it stops for anyone who asks for reduced motion. The first engine is archived as `site/_archive/map-engine-v1.js`.
- **The skills page is a library.** Folders are the fourteen stages, with live counts in a rail; rows are skills, one line each. A row opens the skill in a drawer from the right, so you can walk the shelf and open five skills without losing your place. The open skill lives in the address as `?skill=<id>`, so deep links, back and refresh all work. The full page per skill remains and is one link away. One detail component renders both, so they cannot disagree.
- **The press was reloaded.** The Riso process stays; the inks are now named colours from Sanzo Wada's *A Dictionary of Color Combinations*: Eupatorium Purple with Corinthian Pink as its tint, Violet Blue with Salvia Blue as its tint, Cream Yellow for the gates, and Cotinga Purple, Olive Green, Plumbeous and Carmine Red for the map's meanings. The rule is flashes, not surfaces: a tint may be a ground, a solid may not, and the black keyline is emphasis only. Soft corners everywhere, grain down to 11%, Syne at 700. The stock did not change. Every contrast figure was recomputed and sits in the tokens; the text steps and links clear AA. [brand/colour.md](brand/colour.md) has the argument.
- **Nothing on the site names a colour any more.** The map engine, the systems engine, both config files and three stylesheets carried hex values that a brand change could not reach. Every one is a token now, and the retired-colour guard in `npm --prefix site run check` knows the fluorescent set, so the old inks cannot creep back.
- **Misregistration retired.** The hero and the closing line were printed three times over, in black, pink and blue, a pixel or two apart. Hard to read and loud, which is the opposite of calm and deliberate; you cannot cut a sheet of paper twice. Display type is now printed once, a size smaller, and the move is gone from the brand tokens and the generated stylesheet, so nothing can reach for it.
- **The brand story, told once.** A new beat under the landing hero: "An idea is a sheet of possibility. Pixie Dust Industries gives teams the structure to shape it into something useful." Origami is the supporting idea behind the house, and it appears here with one restrained folded sheet and nowhere else; the boundaries (sparingly, no cranes, no broad cultural styling, never perfection) are written into [brand/positioning.md](brand/positioning.md).
- **The real domain.** `pixiedustindustries.com` is attached to the Vercel project, with `www` redirecting to the apex. The DNS records at the registrar are the remaining step, listed in the audit's hand-over.
- **Not team-visible beyond the site itself:** no skill changed. The count stays at 45.

changelog.title: The QA family, testing the built product and gating the release (45 skills)
changelog.heading: 2026-10-02 – The QA family, testing the built product and gating the release (45 skills)
changelog.body:
The OS tested decisions well and the built product not at all. Every quality skill ran before build (the councils, `grill-my-prd`) or after launch (`metrics-review`). Between "the spec is right" and "the numbers moved" there was nothing, and that gap is where September's QA was done by hand: the price list schedule test that found a Sat/Sun schedule deleted every other schedule, the independent verification that failed a build the councils had passed, the PR-1095 persona session, and the 71-finding Menus 2.0 UAT consolidation. Good work, all improvised. This codifies it, from the QA Skill Family proposal (1 Oct 2026).

- **Eleven new skills.** Two engines: `test-basis` (lines up PRD, stories, decisions, meetings, Figma and code before anyone tests; surfaces dated conflicts, untestable ACs and unmeasurable metrics; rates every flow Frequency × Consequence) and `defect-writer` (one finding standard, de-duped, themed and routed). Seven specialists: `functional-qa`, `exploratory-qa`, `code-qa`, `design-conformance`, `accessibility-audit`, `persona-uat`, `uat-session-kit`. One later-phase specialist, `resilience-qa`, shipped now and honest about the fixtures it still needs. One orchestrator, `qa-mission`, the quality gate.
- **No oracle, no defect.** Every finding cites the source that says it is wrong: an AC, a decision, a WCAG criterion, a component rule, a glossary entry, a PRD metric. Without one it is a Decision needed for a person, never a Bug.
- **Routing follows how the team works.** Before merge, a failed AC sends the story back for rework: a drafted comment to the engineer and the rework transition, and no new ticket, because linked tickets on a story still in rework are how an epic ends up with thousands. After merge, in Dev or Prod, findings become themed Bugs (what was missed) and Improvements (minor). **QA never creates Stories**: new functionality is a requirement gap handed to the PO. Every write waits for a yes.
- **One QA Review page per epic, under the PRD.** What was tested, by whom, when, and the result per AC (Pass, Fail, Blocked, Not tested), plus the quality checks, run log, verdict history and lessons. No page per run.
- **Designed to be optimised, and proven in the market.** `test-basis` checks every PRD success metric can actually be measured (metric, behaviour, event, query, baseline); `functional-qa` confirms the events fire. `qa-mission`'s verdict carries a market handoff: GTM may claim only what QA verified, known issues are said plainly, and `metrics-review` is told what to measure and when. `gtm-handover` now reads it before writing any proof; `metrics-review` starts from its readiness note; `write-prd`'s success metrics must survive the measurability chain.
- **Builder and checker are different.** An agent that saw none of the planning re-checks every P0 and P1, and at Full tier every claimed pass on a high-consequence flow. Synthetic findings resting on drag, hover or timing are capped at "needs human repro". Synthetic UAT is a filter, never sign-off.
- **It learns.** `qa-mission` learn mode traces escapes to the question that missed them, computes escape rate, verification overturn rate, synthetic-to-real prediction and source yield, and proposes amendments to the reference pack for approval. The same numbers decide when a skill earns autonomy.
- **Built mode for both councils.** `design-council-review` and `operator-council-review` now review the live build, not just a mockup. No new skill.
- **The reference pack, `oolio-pm/references/qa/`.** The quality model, oracles (HICCUPPS), risk model, test design techniques, exploration (charters, SFDPOT, tours), severity and defect standard, finding schema, routing, the QA Review page, WCAG 2.2 accessibility standard with proposed surface targets, component reference (Select and ControlBar, more to come with Design), pattern library and glossary grounded in the decision log, hospitality conditions library, device matrix, environment register, browser method, measurability, market handoff, and the learning loop. Facts come from the Brain with their sources; what is proposed or unsettled is marked so, and cited as such.
- **New personas.** The **Quality Bench** (`personas-library/quality-bench/`): eleven testing lenses (Bach and Bolton, Hendrickson, Crispin and Gregory, Adzic, Kaner, Nygard, Watson, Pickering, Frost, Curtis, Krug), the same convention as the Design Council, never invented quotes. **Test persona cards** (`personas-library/test-personas/`): ten behavioural cards on top of the UAT panel, four lifted from the PR-1095 session (Mia, Dave, Priya, Jordan) and six new, each field marked observed or test assumption.
- **Decisions still Niel's, defaulted rather than blocked on:** the gate is advisory until made binding; the reference pack lives in the plugin (the vault is a reference, not a home for it); the accessibility surface targets are proposed; the named lenses are kept. Each is stated where it applies.
- **Tested and pressure-tested before shipping**, recorded in [docs/qa-family-test-record-2026-10-02.md](docs/qa-family-test-record-2026-10-02.md). A routing test routed 12 of 12 findings as expected. A back-test, planning blind from a neutral brief, targeted 7 of the 10 defects the August price list schedule test found and partly targeted the other 3. An adversarial review raised 38 findings (7 Critical), and all were fixed before shipping: escalations are now drafted, never sent; autonomy never covers an external write; a suspected P0 blocks Ship; GTM can read only the current verdict's handoff; rework waits for verification.
- **A new permanent lint, `scripts/check-skills.mjs`,** now part of `npm --prefix site run check`. It fails on descriptions over 950 characters (the silent Cowork drop), unresolved plugin paths and links, mismatched names, per-skill versions, and em dashes in the QA family. Its first run caught `jpd-idea-groomer` at 963 characters, over the ceiling, trimmed here.
- **Counts and catalogues.** 34 → **45**. Manifests, both READMEs, the catalogue (a new Quality & Release stage), `pm-compass` routing, and the site: a new **Quality** column on the map with a **Ship call** gate, a "Spec → Tested → Proven" flow, a loop from measurement back to QA, and an eighth crew member, the Inspector, on the landing page.

changelog.title: push-to-brain: the end of a session becomes a diff against the Brain (34 skills)
changelog.heading: 2026-09-22 — push-to-brain: the end of a session becomes a diff against the Brain (34 skills)
changelog.body:
Sessions end and what they settled evaporates, or it lands as a new file that summarises the chat and that nothing links to. The vault has 599 pages like that. **push-to-brain** is the explicit end-of-session push: it treats the conversation as a diff against what the Brain already holds and makes the smallest change that leaves the right existing note correct.

- **Append, edit, update, insert, and only then create.** In that order, and each with one shape, so two sessions a month apart leave a page that reads as one page. Creation is the last resort and has to pass the vault's birth gate: frontmatter first, a type in the vocabulary, and at least one inbound link before the skill moves on.
- **It runs only when you ask it to.** By name, or by saying to push the session to the Brain. Never on a schedule, never chained from another skill, never because a chat got long. It works only from the conversation and the agent outputs visible in it, and the receipt says so; it never claims to have reviewed something it could not see.
- **Four marks, and none of them promote themselves.** Every kept line is Decided, Proposed, Assumed or Open, dated, and cites a real source when the session had one, otherwise the session. A proposal nobody answered stays a proposal on every re-run.
- **Supersede, never stack.** A decision the session overturns gets a new page with the reasoning and a "supersedes" line; the old page is marked superseded and links forward. A corrected claim keeps its old wording as a dated history note. Nothing is deleted, which was already the vault's rule.
- **Running it twice writes nothing the second time.** It looks for its own footprint first, then checks every item against the destination by phrase before writing (`brain-locate.mjs has`), then checks that no existing heading already covers a section it would insert. The POS domain README carrying two `## Signals received` headings is the failure this prevents.
- **A read-only helper does the fragile half.** `scripts/brain-locate.mjs` ranks the work-layer pages that already cover a topic (canonical pages above the ledger), proves a phrase is or is not on a page, runs the birth gate on a page, and answers whether a path is behind the work/personal wall. It never writes, and it excludes the Personal layers before scoring, so the wall is enforced by the tool rather than by discipline.
